perf.summary: Same double-division of (r2 - r) as in Crt: '% g' then '/ g' on the same operands.
perf.currentCost: Line 23 '(r2 - r) % g' and line 25 '(r2 - r) / g' issue two 64-bit divisions on the same dividend; this runs once per modulus merged (len-1 times per Excrt call).
perf.proposedChange: long delta = r2 - r; long q = delta / g; if (q * g != delta) return false; then ModMul.Run(x, q, m2_g). Single division + multiply-compare.
perf.rationale: Eliminates one 64-bit division per merge iteration, replacing it with a cheap multiply for the divisibility test. Identical result by the same q*g==delta equivalence as in Crt.
perf.risk: q*g == delta fits in long by construction (no overflow). Equality test is sign-agnostic. Behavior of the failure path (return false) is preserved exactly.

perf.summary: TryMerge is a private static helper but not marked AggressiveInlining, unlike sibling hot methods.
perf.currentCost: Called in the inner loop of Run (len-1 times). Without the inline hint Burst may keep it as a call with ref-parameter spills to memory for r and m.
perf.proposedChange: Add [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] to TryMerge so r and m stay in registers across the merge and the call overhead in the loop is removed.
perf.rationale: Inlining the single-call-site helper lets the compiler keep the accumulator state (r, m) in registers instead of round-tripping through the ref parameters, and removes per-iteration call/return overhead.
perf.risk: None semantically. Inlining a recursive-free leaf-ish helper is safe; only watch that the y out-var from ExtendedGcd inside it remains allocated (it's already dead and can be dropped if the RunX variant from the ExtendedGcd opportunity is adopted).
